en: Jātaka:
Miscellaneous Section,
Chapter on the Rice Field of Śāli Rice.
4. The Uddālakajātaka:
“Those with rough antelope skins, matted hair, and mud-stained teeth, who mutter mantras while their appearance is wretched;”
“Surely you have escaped from the states of misery, O wise one, by avoiding human contrivances?
“O King, do not commit evil deeds.”
If one who is learned does not practice the Dhamma,
even one with a thousand-fold knowledge will not, by relying on that,
be released from suffering without having attained right conduct.
“Even one who has mastered the thousand [hymns] is not released from suffering by relying on that, unless he attains right conduct;
I consider the Vedas to be fruitless.”
“Conduct accompanied by self-restraint is indeed the truth.
“The Vedas are not without fruit;
conduct accompanied by self-restraint is indeed the truth.”
“Indeed, one attains fame by mastering the Vedas;
the self-controlled person purifies peace through their conduct.
“Mother, father, and kinsmen are merely sources of sustenance.”
He by whom one is born is indeed oneself;
I am Uddālaka, sir,
born of a lineage of Sottiya brahmins.
“How, sir, does one become a brahmin?
How does one become a perfected one (kevalin)?
And how is there final nibbāna?”
“How is one said to be ‘established in the Dhamma’?
“Having set aside the fire, the brahmin takes it up again;
sprinkling water, he performs the sacrifice and raises the sacrificial post.”
“Acting thus, one is a brahmin who dwells in safety;
therefore, they have declared that he who stands firm in the Dhamma has attained purification.
There is no purity through sprinkling.”
Nor is he a solitary Brahmin;
he possesses neither patience nor gentleness,
nor has he attained final Nibbāna.
“How does one become a brahmin?
How does one become perfected?
And how is there final nibbāna?”
How is one called "established in the Dhamma"?
One who has no kinship with the field of sense-pleasures, who is without "mine-ness," free from longing,
devoid of greed and evil, and whose craving for existence is exhausted.
Acting thus, he is a brahmin who dwells in safety;
therefore, they have honored him as one established in the Dhamma.
"The khattiyas, brahmins, and vessas..."
The Suddas, Caṇḍālas, and Pukkusas—
all are gentle and tamed,
all have attained final nibbāna.
"For all those who have become cool,
there is one who is better and one who is worse.
"The khattiyas, the brahmins, the vessas..."
Śūdras, Caṇḍālas, and Pukkusas—
all are gentle and tamed,
all have attained final Nirvāṇa.
"For all those who have become cool,
there is neither superior nor inferior.
"The khattiyas, brahmins, and vessas..."
Śūdras, Caṇḍālas, and Pukkusas—
all are gentle and tamed,
all have attained final Nirvāṇa.
For all who have become cooled,
there is neither superior nor inferior;
you practice the holy life for the sake of living beings.
The lineage of the Sottiya clan.
"The celestial mansion is covered with cloths of various colors;"
The shadow of those robes did not follow that passion;
even so among humans—
When young men are purified,
having understood the Dhamma and being well-trained in their vows, they release their fellow clansmen.
The Uddālakajātaka is the fourth.
